summary: Begbie lookout beside Highway 97 south of 100 Mile House, BC: a lookout here since 1923, current tower from the 1970s, now a short public trail and recreation site.

facts.design: Two-storey wooden lookout building with a wraparound deck (directory description); a blog says the current tower was built in the 1970s

staffing.status: no longer manned; BC relies on aerial patrols and cameras

access.note: Official recreation site since 2011; short trail from a large gravel parking lot; toilets and picnic tables at base and top

visit.trail_note: Steep rocky trail to the top, about 5 to 10 minutes, or an easier service road to the base of the building; the trail is rough with loose rocks and exposed roots

events.note: Lookout station on the site from 1923 (a working summer lookout); the sources do not say when the first structure went up.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The blog gives 1923 for the lookout here, and the directory gives a 1923 working lookout station. They agree on 1923 and do not say whether the 1923 station was the first structure.

notes_for_editor: Only two travel sites were readable, and neither is an official source. The BC Sites and Trails record (REC160875) came back empty from fetch_text and from WebFetch, so no government source is cited. The Firelookout.ca record has N/A for tower type, height and year. A CampGuide listing (campguide.ca) and a BC Forest Fire Lookouts Facebook post were seen only as search snippets, and they conflict (early 1970s versus 1920s). Neither page was read, so neither is cited, and the building's construction date is unsettled. The 1970s date for the current tower comes from the blog alone. Elevation 1,276 m is from the blog and the directory; the record has no elevation key. No new photos. Before publishing, look for a BC government or heritage source for construction dates and current status.
